newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe fuel prices rise by up to 24 percent.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe fuel prices rise by up to 24 percent.

text.p: Zimbabwe raised the retail price of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products on Friday by up to 24 percent, saying this was necessary to keep local fuel procuring companies viable.

The permanent secretary in the Ministry of Transport and Energy, Paul Kodzwa, said in a statement he believed the price increase -- the second in four months -- would be comfortably absorbed by the economy, expected to grow by over five percent this year.
Petrol went up 12 percent to Z$511 a litre, diesel rose 16 percent to Z$403 a litre and the cost of liquid petroleum gas jumped 24 percent to Z$793 per kg.

"The price review takes into account the increases required to cover losses by the oil industry...and the need to restore viability. I believe the economy can afford to absorb the increases under the current economic conditions," Kodzwa said.
